classification.reasoning: Purpose: The crate has almost no meaningful code (7 lines in build.rs, 1 rust file, 8 meaningful lines total). Sources: It checks the `GITHUB_ACTIONS` environment variable via `env::var("GITHUB_ACTIONS").is_ok()`. Sinks: It attempts a TCP connection to localhost (`127.0.0.1:4001`) inside `build.rs`. Flows: The build script conditionally probes for a CI/CD environment (GitHub Actions) and connects to a local port. Anomalies: Connecting to a local port when executed under CI/CD is characteristic of environment fingerprinting or testing whether specific services/interceptors are active in a pipeline, echoing patterns seen in sandbox evasion or CI-targeted payloads (though here directed at loopback). Conclusion: While connecting to `127.0.0.1` is not direct exfiltration to an external C2, conditionally executing network behavior based on `GITHUB_ACTIONS` in a near-empty crate is highly anomalous and suspicious.

retrieved_context.title: General pattern: legitimate build.rs signals that are NOT malicious
retrieved_context.text: Common benign reasons a crate's build.rs may trigger a raw signal match: checking the installed rustc/cargo version via Command::new (used by serde and many other major crates to gate feature availability); generating code from a schema or protobuf definition, sometimes fetched over network from a first-party, well-known source; reading a small number of standard, non-sensitive environment variables like OUT_DIR, TARGET, or CARGO_PKG_VERSION which Cargo itself sets. A high-quality classifier should not flag these alone -- context (destination of network calls, sensitivity of specific env var names read, and the crate's stated purpose) matters more than raw signal presence.
retrieved_context.source: synthesized from observed benign build.rs behavior, e.g. serde

retrieved_context.title: TrapDoor campaign (May 2026)
retrieved_context.text: A cross-ecosystem attack campaign using build.rs as the Rust-specific execution vector (alongside equivalent hooks in other ecosystems). Demonstrated that the build.rs attack surface is actively being operationalized by organized threat actors, not just opportunistic individuals. Attack category: build.rs as a deliberate cross-ecosystem attack vector, part of a broader coordinated campaign.

retrieved_context.title: CrateDepression / rustdecimal (2022)
retrieved_context.text: A coordinated typosquatting campaign where the crate 'rustdecimal' impersonated the legitimate 'rust_decimal' crate (52M+ downloads at the time). Edit distance from the target name was 1 (removed underscore). The malicious crate's build.rs deployed a Mythic C2 (command and control) agent specifically into GitLab CI/CD pipelines. The payload fingerprinted the environment before activating -- it only deployed inside detected CI systems, evading casual local testing. Attack category: typosquatting + backdoor + CI-targeting build.rs payload.
